texts: bad: "come to a slow boil" makes the result a state NOUN, which forces the change-of-phase shape whose mandatory flat half says each cauldron IS a boil — a false atom — and the result was dropped at group level entirely, so at top level the parse says only that the cauldrons "came", which reads as motion. Put the result in a verb instead: "The cauldrons begin to boil slowly." — the boiling then becomes its own event for each cauldron, the inchoative "come to" survives as the beginning, and nothing types a cauldron as a boil.

mixed: the keeping event, the reified steady simmer and the continuation marker are all right, but "at a steady simmer" is a state noun, so the per-cauldron half comes out as "each cauldron is a simmer", which is false. Say the result with a verb form: "Hesper keeps the cauldrons simmering steadily." — that preserves the maintenance sense and the steadiness while giving each cauldron a simmering event rather than the simmer as its type.

good. the indefinite "a hard boil" correctly stays one witness instead of becoming a generic, hard_boil unpacks into its boil genus and its hard modifier, and ruin gets its agent and its destroyed object.

good. adjudicated accept — every atom is true and well typed; the of-phrase is folded into the slick's own typing (the slick IS the poor essence) only because a portion-of-a-mass phrase has no dedicated form in the instruction set yet.

good. the group event plus a fireable per-thread rule, with the manner adverb and the afternoon time carried on both; only the span sense of "through" flattens to a plain afternoon time, and no rewrite recovers that, so the wording is fine as it stands.

mixed: the rule is fireable and every participant is covered, but "late afternoon" is a modified day-part, so the deadline lands on a coined symbol (late_afternoon) that no time question can order against the recognized ones (dawn, noon, evening, night). If the exact band is not essential, write "By evening a dark slick forms at the bottom of each cauldron." — that gives a comparable time value, at the cost of a slightly later deadline; otherwise keep your wording and accept an opaque time.

mixed: the slick, its precursor typing and the mire-essence link are all recorded, but the link is attached with the wrong head — "precursor" is a relational noun like "tributary of", so it belongs in the ordinary opaque genitive, and as emitted the standard "what is X the precursor of?" query will not find it. A minimal edit that sidesteps the routing is "The slick is the precursor to mire-essence."; if you would rather have the relation as a stated event, "Mire-essence forms from the slick." also parses cleanly.
